first_mine.title: THE GOLD RUSH
first_mine.info: In the 1850's the discovery of Australia's gold, firstly in Ophir NSW, to Ballarat and Bendigo Creek in Victoria, sent people from all over the world to explore and seek riches. From Asia to Europe people raced, transforming the Australian colonies as we know them today.
first_mine.source: National Museum Australia. (2024). Gold Rushes | National Museum of Australia. Nma.gov.au. https://www.nma.gov.au/defining-moments/resources/gold-rushes

buy_license.title: THE COMPULSORY LICENSE
buy_license.info: “The police charged with enforcing the license system were notorious for corruption and for their brutal methods.” They were £1.5, or ~$150 in today's money, and had to be renewed every month otherwise you could be fined or arrested.
buy_license.source: Britannica. (n.d.). Australian gold rushes | Australian history. Encyclopedia Britannica. https://www.britannica.com/event/Australian-gold-rushes

jail.title: THE JAILS
jail.info: If diggers were caught without a license, they were chained together, or tied down till they were collected, led to the government camp. They were then forced to pay a £5 fine, ~1,400 AUD, otherwise they were taken to jail. The aftermath of the Eureka Stockade led to many diggers cramped into jail cells. The above image was a portable jail cell, commonly used at the time.

buy_pan.title: TIN PAN ALLEY
buy_pan.info: Panning was the simplest form of mining. Diggers swirled gravel in water, hoping heavy gold would settle at the bottom.

buy_pickaxe.title: DEEP LEAD MINING
buy_pickaxe.info: As surface gold vanished, miners dug vertical shafts hundreds of feet deep. These were incredibly dangerous.

buy_cradle.title: THE ROCKING CRADLE
buy_cradle.info: A cradle allowed a team to process ten times more dirt than a pan by washing soil through riffles.

buy_puddling.title: PUDDLING MACHINES
buy_puddling.info: Puddling used horses to break down heavy clay, allowing for industrial-scale gold separation.

rebellion.title: THE SOUTHERN CROSS OATH
rebellion.info: Miners swore to stand truly by each other and fight to defend their rights under the Southern Cross flag.

welcome_stranger.title: THE WELCOME STRANGER
welcome_stranger.info: Discovered in 1869, this 72kg nugget is the largest ever found. It had to be broken on an anvil to be weighed.

police_raid.title: THE LICENSE HUNTS
police_raid.info: Police (known as 'Joes') conducted aggressive hunts for licenses, often leading to violent confrontations.
